cases.name: Linda Lee Kilgore Kincade Curry
cases.about: She worked at the San Onofre nuclear power plant.
cases.narrative:
He slowly poisoned her over the course of a year by putting tobacco in her salad dressing before he finally slipped her a powerful sedative Ambien and injected her with a fatal dose of nicotine behind her ear. She was a nonsmoker, but tests revealed fatal levels of nicotine in her system.

cases.name: Jacque Joann “Jacqwelyn” Villagomez
cases.about:
Her Find-a-Grave said, "Jacque was born in Modesto, California to Geri Bonnell and Edward Joseph Villagomez. She attended Brown Elementary School, Turlock Junior High, and Pitman High Schools before moving to Southern California where she graduated from El Toro High School in Orange County. This beautiful young woman was a star athlete at Pitman High where she still holds school records in the hurdle events. She was a
multi-talented young woman with a brilliant smile and a kind and trusting heart. When she wasn't on the track, she enjoyed drama, singing and dancing. Jacque had a zest for life." 

(She) was a high-school track star in hurdles, loved to act, sing and dance, and her goal was to become a model. After high school, she moved out to pursue her dreams, and she worked as a waitress and landed some modeling jobs, Sevino said.
